fixtures.title: Mutual confidentiality agreement
fixtures.purpose: Small, extractable agreement with reciprocal obligations, exceptions and a survival period.

sections.heading: 1. Parties and purpose
sections.text: Example Customer and Example Supplier wish to evaluate a fictional document-review project. Either party may disclose confidential information for that purpose. This synthetic agreement starts on 1 January 2026.

sections.heading: 2. Confidential information
sections.text: Confidential information means non-public project plans, pricing and technical material identified as confidential when shared. It excludes information already public, independently developed, or lawfully received without a confidentiality duty.

sections.heading: 3. Reciprocal obligations
sections.text: Each receiving party must use the information only for the stated purpose, protect it with reasonable care, and share it only with representatives who need it and have equivalent confidentiality obligations.

sections.heading: 4. Required disclosure
sections.text: If disclosure is legally required, the receiving party may disclose the required portion and, where permitted, notify the disclosing party before disclosure.

sections.heading: 5. Term and return
sections.text: Either party may end discussions with written notice. On request, each party must return or delete the other party's confidential information, except one restricted archival copy. The confidentiality obligation survives for two years after the discussions end.

sections.heading: 6. No further commitment
sections.text: Neither party is required to enter another agreement. Each party retains its existing intellectual property. No signature, personal information or real transaction is represented by this test document.

sections.heading: 1. Scope
sections.text: Example Supplier will prepare a fictional document inventory for Example Customer. The engagement starts on 1 February 2026. Deliverables and charges appear in Schedule A on page 2.

sections.heading: 2. Fees and payment
sections.text: Invoices are payable within 30 days of receipt. Charges are stated in GBP. See Schedule A for the invoice schedule. This clause contains no priority rule resolving a difference between this clause and Schedule A.

sections.heading: 3. Acceptance
sections.text: Example Customer has ten business days after delivery to identify a material failure against the written scope. Example Supplier will correct an identified failure and resubmit the deliverable.

sections.heading: 4. Term and ending the work
sections.text: The engagement lasts three months. Either party may end it with 14 days of written notice. Example Customer must pay for work completed before the end date. Confidentiality duties continue for one year after the engagement ends.

sections.heading: 5. Responsibility
sections.text: Example Supplier's total liability is limited to fees paid under this agreement. Example Customer's payment obligations are not subject to that limit. These fictional terms are included for review experimentation, not as a legal recommendation.

sections.heading: A1. Delivery schedule
sections.text: The table below forms part of the scope described in clause 1. All dates, charges and deliverables are invented.

after_table.heading: A2. Invoice timing
after_table.text: Example Supplier may invoice when each deliverable is submitted. Each invoice is payable within 7 days of receipt. Clause 2 on page 1 also states a payment deadline; the difference is intentional in this synthetic fixture.

after_table.heading: A3. Change requests
after_table.text: A change to the scope, delivery dates or charges requires written agreement by both parties before the additional work starts.
